title: Smart retry ledger and idempotency adapter for SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Ship a compact, cross-language "smart retry ledger" and an "idempotency adapter" across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that: (1) provides safe default retry/backoff profiles for both unary and streaming calls, (2) exposes ergonomic idempotency helpers that integrate with the ledger for dedupe and resume, and (3) emits telemetry for dedupe and retry classification. This ticket coordinates the design, per-language API surface, migration path, integration tests, and an initial rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs publish a stable helper (RetryLedger) that records attempt metadata and returns a canonical retry decision for unary and streaming requests
Idempotency adapter provides a 1-line wrapper for request/response flows that automatically attaches id-key, TTL, and local dedupe with fallback to persistent ledger
Streaming resume uses chunk-level sequence IDs + ledger to safely resume only idempotent chunks; documented examples for Python, TS, and Go included
Default retry profiles (fast, balanced, conservative) implemented and wired to telemetry with clear labels
End-to-end integration tests exercising duplicate-suppression, stream-resume, and cost-aware aborts present in CI
PRs merged for python-sdk, ts-sdk, go-sdk and sample app demonstrating user migration guide
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use a small client-side ledger (pluggable persistence) rather than global server-side dedupe to avoid high-cardinality server state and to support offline/offload scenarios

Default backoff algorithm: capped exponential backoff with configurable full-jitter; we expose three presets (fast=short cap, balanced=medium, conservative=long) to cover most workloads rather than indefinite auto-tuning at launch
Idempotency key format: stable namespace <sdk>.<env>.<operation>.<user-provided-id> serialized as URL-safe base64; prevents accidental collisions and is easy for customers to inspect

Streaming resume opt-in by default for chunked uploads/long-poll patterns because resume semantics are tricky for non-idempotent operations; when enabled, SDK attaches per-chunk checksums and ledger entries
Cost-aware retries: for requests estimated above a token-cost threshold (e.g., long generation), ledger returns 'no-retry' by default to avoid unexpected spend; customers can override
We will avoid binary protocol changes; all behavior achieved in SDKs and server-compatible metadata headers to maintain backward compatibility
implementation_tasks: Design core RetryLedger interface and persistence adapter (memory, sqlite, redis) - core library (shared psuedo-spec)
Implement idempotency adapter for Python with context manager and decorator samples
Implement idempotency adapter for TypeScript with middleware and fetch wrapper
Implement idempotency adapter for Go with http.RoundTripper and streaming chunk helper
Add telemetry events: retry_attempt, retry_classified, dedupe_hit, dedupe_miss, resume_attempt
Write e2e tests (dup request, stream resume, high-cost abort) and add to cross-sdk CI
Docs: migration guide, API reference, example apps
Security review for persisting id-keys in optional persistence backends (if enabled)

2025-11-07 Diego Alvarez: Proposed base64-url id-key format and suggested including operation fingerprint to reduce collisions
2025-11-10 UX (Priya Rao): Suggest we expose a single high-level helper per SDK to keep ergonomics consistent across languages

2025-11-13 Engineering sync: Agreed to emit header X-RW-Idempotency-Key and X-RW-Resume-Chunk to allow server-side correlation; keep behavior safe if server ignores headers
2025-11-15 Diego Alvarez: Pushed python prototype (GH PR #2345) for early feedback
2025-11-17 Maya Chen: Ran local perf microbenchmarks; in-memory ledger latency <1ms for common ops, sqlite persistence adds ~2-3ms on cold path

examples:
// Go example:
ledger := retryledger.New(retryledger.WithSQLite('/tmp/rw_ledger.db'))
httpClient := idempotency.NewClient(http.DefaultClient, ledger, "chat.create", 3600)
resp, err := httpClient.Post(...)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): release python helper as opt-in with memory-only ledger + docs; announce to early access SDK users
Phase 2: ship TS and Go implementations; add sqlite persistence adapters and CI tests
Phase 3: enable telemetry and default balanced retry profile; add migration guide and sample app
Phase 4 (enterprise): document redis persistence and configuration for Dedicated/Private deployments; recommend sales/SE talking points
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Ledger growth and privacy concerns if persisted unknowingly - Mitigation: ledger persistence opt-in, encryption guidance in docs
Risk: Customers rely on resume for non-idempotent operations - Mitigation: resume is opt-in and requires explicit per-chunk checksum and opt-in flag
Risk: Additional cost from retries on large generations - Mitigation: cost-aware default prevents retries above token-cost threshold; customers can override
notes: Telemetry schema draft: event.retry.attempt {reason: transient|throttling|timeout, profile: fast|balanced|conservative, attempt: int}
We should coordinate header naming with backend team (Pablo Torres) before finalizing X-RW-* headers
Follow-up: evaluate adaptive backoff in 2026 if usage patterns show clear benefits
